_meta.status: DEMO - NOT APPROVED FOR CLINICAL OR OPERATIONAL USE
_meta.purpose: Structure and traceability demonstration for ARES protocol retrieval. Real flight medical procedures (e.g., ISS medical checklists) are controlled documents and are not public. In a real system every entry below would be replaced by flight-surgeon-approved procedures with document IDs, revisions and sign-off.
_meta.policy: ARES only RETRIEVES and DISPLAYS entries from this file verbatim. It never generates, edits or combines medical instructions.

protocols.title: Verify an abnormal reading before acting
protocols.triggers: abnormal reading sensor check verify re-measure artifact flatline lead off probe contact
assessment_steps: Ask the crew member how they feel; note any symptoms.
Check sensor placement and contact (oximeter probe, ECG electrodes, belt).
Re-measure with the redundant/backup device where available.
Compare with the crew member's personal baseline shown by ARES.
protocols.escalation_criteria: Escalate per the relevant protocol if the abnormal value is confirmed on a second device or symptoms are present.

source.title: ARES design principle: sensor-failure-safe escalation (this project)

protocols.title: Low oxygen saturation - initial assessment
protocols.triggers: low spo2 desaturation hypoxaemia oxygen saturation shortness of breath breathing difficulty
assessment_steps: Confirm the reading (GEN-01): reposition probe, check perfusion, use backup oximeter.
Check cabin atmosphere telemetry (ppO2, ppCO2) - an environmental cause affects the whole crew.
Assess breathing rate, effort, and level of alertness.
Notify the Crew Medical Officer (CMO) immediately.
Prepare onboard oxygen equipment per the vehicle's APPROVED procedure; administration only per CMO/flight-surgeon protocol.
protocols.escalation_criteria: Critical: SpO2 persistently below the critical limit, altered alertness, or worsening despite approved interventions.

source.title: O'Driscoll BR et al. BTS guideline for oxygen use in adults in healthcare and emergency settings. Thorax 2017;72(Suppl 1)

protocols.title: Irregular or fast heart rhythm - initial assessment
protocols.triggers: arrhythmia irregular rhythm tachycardia palpitations atrial fibrillation fast heart rate ecg abnormal
assessment_steps: Confirm with a manual pulse check and the ECG trace (rule out lead artefact).
Record a longer, multi-lead ECG if the equipment allows.
Ask about symptoms: palpitations, chest pain, dizziness, breathlessness.
Measure blood pressure now (do not wait for the scheduled cuff cycle).
Notify the CMO; queue the ECG strip for flight-surgeon review.
protocols.escalation_criteria: Critical: chest pain, fainting, low blood pressure, or heart rate beyond the critical limit at rest.

source.title: Generic first-response assessment structure (placeholder for flight-surgeon procedure)

protocols.title: Fever with raised heart/breathing rate - screening
protocols.triggers: fever temperature infection sepsis febrile chills raised heart rate breathing
assessment_steps: Confirm temperature with a second method.
Screen with qSOFA criteria: respiratory rate >= 22/min, systolic BP <= 100 mmHg, altered mentation.
Look for a source (respiratory, urinary, skin, wound) and ask about symptoms.
Isolate shared items if infection is suspected; notify the CMO.
Track trend every 15 min; ARES will show the rate of change.
protocols.escalation_criteria: Medical assessment if qSOFA >= 2 or deterioration across multiple systems.

source.title: Singer M et al. The Third International Consensus Definitions for Sepsis and Septic Shock (Sepsis-3). JAMA 2016;315(8):801-810

protocols.title: Suspected fluid deficit (dehydration) - assessment
protocols.triggers: dehydration fluid loss low blood pressure tachycardia dizziness thirst urine
assessment_steps: Review recent fluid intake, exercise load, vomiting or heat exposure.
Measure BP and heart rate now; repeat in 15 min.
Ask about dizziness, headache, thirst; check urine output/colour if logged.
Notify the CMO; follow the APPROVED fluid-replacement procedure only on CMO direction.
protocols.escalation_criteria: Medical assessment if BP keeps falling, heart rate keeps rising, or symptoms appear.

source.title: Generic assessment structure (placeholder for flight-surgeon procedure)

protocols.title: Sleep debt and fatigue - countermeasure review
protocols.triggers: fatigue sleep deprivation tired insomnia sleep debt low hrv workload
assessment_steps: Review the crew member's sleep over the past 72 h (ARES timeline).
Review workload and schedule; consider protecting the next sleep period.
Check sleep environment: noise, light, temperature, CO2.
Avoid assigning safety-critical tasks during peak fatigue where the schedule allows; inform the Commander.
protocols.escalation_criteria: Report to the flight surgeon at the next communication window if the trend persists > 3 days.

source.title: NASA Human Research Program: Risk of performance decrements and adverse health outcomes resulting from sleep loss, circadian desynchronization and work overload (HRP evidence report)

protocols.title: Solar particle event - crew protection
protocols.triggers: solar particle event radiation storm shelter dose spike sep proton flux
assessment_steps: Move all crew to the designated storm shelter per the vehicle flight rule.
Confirm every crew member's dosimeter is worn and logging.
Suspend EVA and non-essential activity in lightly shielded areas.
Monitor dose rate; remain sheltered until the flight rule's all-clear criteria are met.
Log event dose per crew member against the 250 mSv SPE limit and the 600 mSv career limit.
protocols.escalation_criteria: Report event dose to ground at the next window; acute symptoms (nausea, vomiting) require medical assessment.

source.title: NASA-STD-3001 Technical Brief OCHMO-TB-020: Design for Ionizing Radiation Protection

protocols.title: Critical emergency - crew response coordination
protocols.triggers: critical emergency unresponsive collapse life threatening escalation all crew
assessment_steps: Alert all crew; CMO leads, Commander coordinates.
Bring the medical kit and backup monitoring to the patient.
Follow the specific approved procedure for the suspected problem.
Send a P1 message to ground immediately - but act locally: ground cannot respond before the round-trip delay shown by ARES.

source.title: ARES design principle: mission-aware autonomy (this project)

protocols.title: Elevated cabin CO2 - crew and vehicle response
protocols.triggers: cabin ppCO2 1-hour average above 3 mmHg; several crew breathing faster at the same time; headaches
assessment_steps: Confirm the reading with a second (portable) CO2 monitor before acting on it.
Check CO2-removal system status and cabin ventilation fans; report to the vehicle systems lead.
Move crew away from poorly ventilated areas (microgravity allows local CO2 pockets).
Reduce or postpone exercise to lower metabolic CO2 output until levels fall.
Ask each crew member about headache, fatigue or blurred vision and log the symptoms in ARES.
Re-check every 15 minutes until the 1-hour average is below 3 mmHg.
escalation_criteria: ppCO2 keeps rising despite the steps above
any crew member with confusion, severe headache or shortness of breath -> treat as medical event (L2)

source.title: NASA-STD-3001 Technical Brief OCHMO-TB-004 Carbon Dioxide; NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2 [V2 6004]

protocols.title: Behavioral readiness - support and countermeasure review
protocols.triggers: behavioral readiness Watch or Support suggested: vigilance decline, high fatigue, mood/stress change, sleep debt
assessment_steps: Private conversation between the crew member and the CMO (results are not shared crew-wide).
Review the sleep schedule, light exposure and workload for the coming days; protect sleep opportunity.
Avoid scheduling safety-critical tasks for this crew member while vigilance is reduced, where possible.
Offer the agreed coping and relaxation resources; encourage contact with family when the link allows.
Request a private conference with the ground behavioral health team in the next communication window.
escalation_criteria: any concern for crew member safety -> CMO + commander immediately

source.title: NASA Human Research Program - Risk of Adverse Cognitive or Behavioral Conditions (behavioral health and performance)
